TDLR: The single player has some cool location concepts, but is unfortunately very lacking in content. Maybe for "Baby's first 3d collect-athon" it would be a good deal. Multiplayer, however, is what saves this game and makes it worth watching out for on sales. It's about as fun as 'Gang Beasts' in that regard.

THE GOOD
The tutorial island and World 2 (snowy mountains) had nice location specific gimmicks
* The story mode maps were all littered with fans of sorts, which might sound off-putting, but getting knocked into the air by air currents was an enjoyable method of travel, I'll admit.
* The multiplayer modes are all very entertaining! There is Delivery (racing), Boxing (arena battle), Thief (Coin battle), Oddbox (Fall Guys' take on Tail Tag), and Collect (Zone Control) 
* The inclusion of Bounce (the character, not the jump feature) made 100%-ing this game far less annoying in the long run, since you could essentially talk to him and deduce the location of various objects with the small camera angle he gives you, instead of wandering aimlessly for potentially hours looking for that stupid last roll of tape. (This is the only point I will give Unbox over "Goat Simulator" in terms of single player, as finding the trophies in that game with no help was almost impossible.)
* Air mobility feels nice. Using the slam button when your'e jumping over slopes feels smooth.

THE BAD
* In both modes, the player camera is not the greatest.
* The story mode is NOT multiplayer. This was to be expected, since collecting 800 gold tapes would be very convenient that way and this story mode hates convenience.
* The multiplayer mode is NOT actually supported online. You must use "remote play" to play with some friends online, which streams your audio and video to them. It's a nitpick, I know, but still.
* In both modes, the hat you are wearing effects the way your character rolls on the ground. This will effect your performance in speedruns and racing mode.
* The actual main story plummets after act 1 of the story mode, but nobody's really here for that.
* Getting off a sled in World 2 crashed my game all 3 times I've tried it. Unboxxing (double jumping) out of the sled however works fine. No idea why this happens. 
* All of the cosmetics in the game are either skins of characters from the story mode or a recolor of a Zippie (this game's take on Toad from the Mario series) which is disheartening to some, since it will mean your character will never truly look like an original work.
* Most of the cosmetic items must be earned in story mode to be used in multiplayer mode, which is extremely lame, since story mode is this game's weakness.
* The main collectible in this game is tape. TAPE??? Really?? These are DELIVERY boxes, the main collectible literally should have been MAIL, it would have made so much sense!!!

Overall, being able to do Steam Remote Play and couch co-op multiplayer on this game makes this game a total winner when it's on sale, and the game typically goes on sale for $5 or even just $3. The story mode even has a few neat ideas for hub worlds for aspiring developers today!

I had the ol’ lockdown blues the past few days so I was really in the mood for a 3D platformer to keep me busy but not take up too much concentration. Unbox: Newbie’s Adventure is a cute casual 3D platformer which I think fit the bill pretty well.

Although it has most of the classic characteristics of an old 90s 3D platformer; bright colourful graphics, hub world, collectables, slightly cheesy story, antagonist and characters, what Unbox does slightly differently is the movement mechanic.
If you haven’t noticed already, you are in fact, a box. You roll around as said box and you only really have one way of navigating the space or doing anything, which is jumping. No crouching, backflipping, wall jumping or any of that stuff you might possibly find in a usual 3D platformer. Newbie just jumps to his lil hearts content. You have a normal jump, but you are also given the ability to double, triple, quadruple jump, etc, upwards of 6 times after your initial jump. This is done by using pickups that you collect in the world (which actually double as your health). This makes it so you have to make sure you are managing your jumps and stocking up on pickups, making the platforming more strategic at times. Being able to jump so much also makes for a quite fun and easy way to get around the maps. It’s a very simple movement mechanic but it makes it all the more casual really and it was something I appreciated whilst playing this in the mood I was in.

In terms of the controls, I would say that it might take a bit to get used to given the above mentioned mechanic, but I never had any issues and always felt in control.

In total there are 3 main levels and a hub area for you to explore. This doesn’t sound a lot, and it isn’t really, but the maps are pretty huge and there are a fair few collectables in each area. Normally in these kind of games the maps are smaller and more concise, but I actually quite enjoyed roaming larger maps for once.
In terms of the collectables, each level includes 200 “golden packing tapes” per area, which is a lot! These are kind of like coins or gems you find in other games, quite common on the maps. What you’re really working towards is collecting stamps. Collecting enough of them in a level lets you take on the boss for that level, and you can progress from there.
Collectables and a large map don’t really sound like they go together too well, so I did have my worries at first knowing how frustrating it can be when you have a big map and you have to search every nook and cranny for one collectable you’ve missed. Thankfully, the game has hints to make it very manageable. If you get really stuck, there is a character you can ask who will show you a small preview of where a collectable is. From the preview you can then try and figure out what is in its surroundings, to determine where it may be.

If you played this game and only got the required amount of collectables to move on, this would be a pretty short game. If you, like me, enjoy 100%ing 3D platformers, it will likely take you a significant amount more time to complete. I would put it in the short/medium range. 
The game felt short to me, I blasted through this game in two days, in two sittings, so I thought it was a really short game but apparently it took me 16.4 hours according to Steam so that isn’t actually [i]that short[/i], I just no-lifed the game a little too hard. In honesty, I was a little sad when I completed it to be honest because I was enjoying how casual this game is.

In terms of difficultly it’s really easy, there are “challenges” in the game but they aren’t very challenging. Usually in these games there is at least one part of it I get frustrated with and it takes me a few tries (e.g. stupid boss fights or higher difficulty timed challenges or races) but there was none of that in Unbox. I could completely understand that maybe some people may see this as too easy, but I guess it just depends on what you are looking for. If you want a casual/easy game it’s great for that, but if you wanted something engaging that gives you a challenge I can see how it may fall short.

Overall I found it to be a fun addition to the genre and I would definitely recommend it.
